kusikiliza silabi za sauti lengwa zikitamkwa na mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au kutoka kwa vifaa vya kidijitali kama vile kinasasauti na rununu,

kuunda vitanzandimi kwenye vifaa vya kidijitali na kushirikiana na wenzake mitamboni kuvirekebisha,

Ubunifu: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika kuunda vitanzandimi.

skills.name: Elewa na tumia msamiati wa kifungu
skills.mastery: Gives the meaning of a word from the sentence it is in and picks the word that fits a gap in a sentence, without choosing a look-alike, a nearby or an opposite word, in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

skills.name: Elewa ujumbe wa kifungu cha hadithi
skills.mastery: Answers who, what and which questions from a short story, puts four events in order, and gives the main message, without choosing a detail for the message or an answer from outside the story, in 8 of 10 new questions.

misconceptions.error: Picks a word that looks or sounds like the word.

example.question: Katika kifungu, neno "mche" lina maana gani?

misconceptions.cause: The child goes by the first letters.
misconceptions.reveals: A look-alike word as an option.
misconceptions.help: Say what each word means.
misconceptions.feedback: Maneno yanaweza kufanana kwa umbo na yasiwe na maana sawa. Mche ni mmea mchanga wa kupanda, si mchele.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks a word from the same sentence, not the word asked.

example.question: Katika kifungu, neno "kuchemsha" lina maana gani?

misconceptions.cause: The child picks the meaning of a nearby action.
misconceptions.reveals: The meaning of the word next to it as an option.
misconceptions.help: Put each meaning in place of the word. Which one fits?
misconceptions.feedback: Jaribu kila maana mahali pa neno hilo. Maana sahihi ndiyo inayofaa sentensi nzima.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks the opposite of the word.

example.question: Katika kifungu, neno "madonge" lina maana gani?

misconceptions.cause: The child knows what the word is about but not which way it points.
misconceptions.reveals: The opposite meaning as an option.
misconceptions.help: Read the sentence again: does it say the thing is there or not?
misconceptions.feedback: Maana ya neno hutegemea sentensi lilimotumika. Madonge ni vipande vilivyoshikana, si unga laini.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Names the wrong person from the story.
misconceptions.cause: The child goes by the name that comes first in the passage.
misconceptions.reveals: A question about who, with other people in the story.
misconceptions.help: Find the sentence that names the person who did it.
misconceptions.feedback: Kifungu kinasema nani alifanya kitendo hicho. Soma sentensi hiyo tena.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives an answer from what the child knows, not from the passage.
misconceptions.cause: The child answers from life and does not look in the text.
misconceptions.reveals: A likely answer that the story does not give.
misconceptions.help: Point to the sentence in the passage that says it.
misconceptions.feedback: Jibu la swali la ufahamu liko kwenye kifungu. Tafuta sentensi inayolisema.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks another detail from the story.
misconceptions.cause: The child picks a detail from the right place but not the one asked.
misconceptions.reveals: Several details from one sentence.
misconceptions.help: Read the question word again: who, when, where, what?
misconceptions.feedback: Maneno ya swali (nani, lini, wapi, nini) yanaonyesha jibu la aina gani. Soma kifungu tena.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives a detail for the main message.

example.question: Ujumbe mkuu wa hadithi ni upi?

misconceptions.cause: The child takes the most vivid detail.
misconceptions.reveals: A detail and a message as options.
misconceptions.help: What did the story want us to learn?
misconceptions.feedback: Ujumbe mkuu ni funzo la hadithi nzima, si jambo moja dogo ndani yake.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts the events in the wrong order.

example.question: Matukio manne yamechanganywa. Yalitokea kwa mpangilio gani?

misconceptions.cause: The child goes by the order in the question and not in the story.
misconceptions.reveals: Four events shown out of order.
misconceptions.help: Find the first event, then the next.
misconceptions.feedback: Hadithi inasimulia matukio kwa mpangilio. Maneno kama "kisha" na "baadaye" husaidia.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kujadili na wenzake maana ya insha ya wasifu,
kutambua insha ya wasifu kwa kurejelea vielelezo vya insha vilivyoandikwa kwenye matini mbalimbali au tarakilishi,
kujadili na wenzake mada ya insha na muundo wa insha ya wasifu,
kuandaa vidokezo vitakavyomwongoza kuandika insha yake,

kuandika insha inayoeleza sifa za mtu kama vile mzazi au mlezi, rafiki, mwalimu au kiongozi yeyote kwa kuzingatia anwani, mpangilio mzuri wa mawazo, hati nadhifu, tahajia, kanuni za kisarufi, uakifishaji mwafaka na kwa ubunifu,
kuandika insha ya wasifu mtandaoni na kuisambaza kwa wenzake na mwalimu ili waisome na kuitathmini.
key_inquiry_questions: Je, unazingatia mambo gani unapoandika insha nzuri ya wasifu?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika mijadala na kazi za vikundi kujadili mada na muundo wa insha ya wasifu.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia kifaa cha kidijitali kuandika na kusambaza insha ya wasifu mtandaoni.
Ubunifu: mwanafunzi anapoandika insha ya wasifu.
Kujiamini: mwanafunzi anapoweza kuandika insha ya wasifu kwa kuzingatia anwani, mpangilio mzuri wa mawazo, hati nadhifu, tahajia, kanuni za kisarufi, uakifishaji mwafaka.
sub_strands.values:
Heshima: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake kujadili mada na muundo wa insha ya wasifu.
Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anapotumia kifaa cha kidijitali kuandika insha na kukitunza.
sub_strands.pcis:
Mshikamano wa kijamii: mwanafunzi anapofanya shughuli za kikundi pamoja na wenzake kwa amani.
Haki za watoto: mwanafunzi anaposoma masuala kuhusu mambo ya nyumbani katika insha au kifungu.
sub_strands.links: Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha stadi ya kuandika insha ya wasifu katika somo hili na ujifunzaji wa dhana hiyo katika somo la English.

outcomes.text: kutambua insha ya wasifu kwa kuzingatia muundo
kuandika insha ya wasifu kwa kuzingatia ujumbe, mtindo na muundo ufaao
kuchangamkia utunzi mzuri wa insha ya wasifu ili kujenga ubunifu wake

skills.name: Tambua insha ya wasifu, masimulizi na maelezo na sehemu za insha
skills.mastery: Names the kind of insha from a short text (wasifu describes a person or thing, masimulizi tells what happened in order, maelezo explains) and the part of an insha (utangulizi, kiini, hitimisho), in 8 of 10 new items.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Calls a text that describes a person or thing a masimulizi.

example.question: Ni insha ya aina gani? "Bibi yangu ni mpole. Ana nywele nyeupe na anapenda kusimulia hadithi."

misconceptions.cause: The child sees that it is about a person and thinks of a story.
misconceptions.reveals: A description of a person.
misconceptions.help: Does the text tell what happened in order, or what the person is like?
misconceptions.feedback: Wasifu humwelezea mtu au kitu: sura, tabia na maisha. Masimulizi husimulia matukio kwa mpangilio.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Calls a text that tells what happened a wasifu.

example.question: Ni insha ya aina gani? "Jumamosi, Achieng alienda sokoni. Mvua ilianza kunyesha, akakimbilia dukani."

misconceptions.cause: The child sees a person and thinks it describes her.
misconceptions.reveals: A story about a person.
misconceptions.help: Is something happening, one thing after another?
misconceptions.feedback: Masimulizi husimulia mambo yaliyotokea kwa mpangilio. Wasifu huelezea jinsi mtu alivyo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Calls a text that explains how to do something a masimulizi.

example.question: Ni insha ya aina gani? "Ili kupika wali, osha mchele kwanza. Kisha chemsha maji."

misconceptions.cause: The child sees steps and reads them as events.
misconceptions.reveals: Instructions that sound like a story.
misconceptions.help: Is it telling what happened, or how to do it?
misconceptions.feedback: Maelezo hueleza jambo au jinsi ya kufanya kitu hatua kwa hatua.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Mixes the parts of an insha (utangulizi, kiini, hitimisho).

example.question: Sehemu ya mwisho ya insha huitwa ___.

misconceptions.cause: The child knows the three names but not their order.
misconceptions.reveals: The three parts asked in turn.
misconceptions.help: Which part comes first, which in the middle, which last?
misconceptions.feedback: Insha ina utangulizi mwanzoni, kiini katikati na hitimisho mwishoni.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tambua na tumia nomino
skills.mastery: Picks the noun (the name of a person, animal, place or thing) from a group of words and a sentence, and fills a gap with a noun, without choosing a verb, an adjective or an adverb, in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.
Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Picks a verb (a word for an action) for a noun.
misconceptions.cause: The child sees a word that goes with the sentence and does not ask what kind of word it is.
misconceptions.reveals: A gap that needs a thing, with a verb among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask: is it the name of something, or something being done?
misconceptions.feedback: Nomino ni jina la mtu, mnyama, mahali au kitu. "Anapika" ni kitenzi, kinaonyesha kitendo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks an adjective (a word that describes) for a noun.
misconceptions.cause: The child picks the word that tells about the thing, not the thing.
misconceptions.reveals: A noun among describing words.
misconceptions.help: Can you hold it, see it or name it? Then it may be a noun.
misconceptions.feedback: Nomino ni jina la kitu chenyewe. "Kubwa" ni kivumishi, kinaeleza kitu kikoje.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks a word of time or manner (haraka, jana, sana) for a noun.
misconceptions.cause: The child picks a short word that fits the sentence.
misconceptions.reveals: A noun among words of time and manner.
misconceptions.help: Does the word name something?
misconceptions.feedback: "Haraka" na "jana" ni vielezi: vinaonyesha jinsi au wakati. Nomino hutaja mtu, mnyama, mahali au kitu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks a noun for a verb.
misconceptions.cause: The child takes the word nearest the gap that names a thing.
misconceptions.reveals: A gap that needs an action, with a noun among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask: what is Juma doing?
misconceptions.feedback: Kitenzi kinaonyesha kitendo: anacheza. "Uwanja" ni nomino, ni jina la mahali.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks an adjective for a verb.
misconceptions.cause: The child picks a word that goes with chakula.
misconceptions.reveals: A gap that needs an action, with a describing word among the options.
misconceptions.help: Can you do the word? Cooking can be done; "kitamu" cannot.
misconceptions.feedback: Kitenzi kinaonyesha kitendo. "Kitamu" ni kivumishi, kinaeleza chakula kikoje.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks a word of time or manner (sasa, mapema) for a verb.

misconceptions.reveals: A gap that needs an action, with a time or manner word.
misconceptions.help: Ask: who does what?
misconceptions.feedback: "Mapema" ni kielezi cha wakati. Kitenzi ni neno la kitendo, kama "wanapanda".
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.mastery: Picks the greeting or farewell that fits the person and the time (hujambo-sijambo, shikamoo-marahaba, habari za asubuhi, kwaheri, usiku mwema), without giving the greeting back as the reply, in 8 of 10 new situations. Using them aloud is a teacher's check.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Gives the greeting back as the reply (Hujambo for Sijambo).
misconceptions.cause: The child repeats the word he heard.
misconceptions.reveals: A greeting and its reply as options.
misconceptions.help: Who is asking, and who answers?
misconceptions.feedback: Hujambo hujibiwa kwa "Sijambo". Shikamoo hujibiwa kwa "Marahaba".
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses a greeting of the wrong time of day (habari za asubuhi at night).

example.question: Kabla ya kulala usiku unamwambia mama, "___."

misconceptions.cause: The child knows the greeting but not when it is used.
misconceptions.reveals: A morning greeting for an evening situation.
misconceptions.help: What time of day is it?
misconceptions.feedback: "Habari za asubuhi" ni ya asubuhi. "Usiku mwema" husemwa usiku kabla ya kulala.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Greets an elder with the greeting for a friend (hujambo for shikamoo).
misconceptions.cause: The child uses one greeting for everyone.
misconceptions.reveals: An elder and a friend as the people greeted.
misconceptions.help: Is the person older than you?
misconceptions.feedback: Mdogo humsalimia mkubwa kwa "Shikamoo", na mkubwa hujibu "Marahaba". "Hujambo" ni ya rika moja.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tumia kamusi: mpangilio wa maneno na maana
skills.mastery: Puts words in the order of the alphabet (using the second and third letters when the first match) and says what a dictionary is for, in 8 of 10 new items.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Looks at the first letter only (words that begin alike).

example.question: Kati ya "samaki", "sahani" na "sufuria", neno linalokuja kwanza ni ___.

misconceptions.cause: The child stops when the first letters are the same.
misconceptions.reveals: Words that begin with the same letter.
misconceptions.help: When the first letters match, look at the second.
misconceptions.feedback: Maneno yakianza kwa herufi moja, tazama herufi ya pili, kisha ya tatu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts the shortest word first.

example.question: Kati ya "ua", "ardhi" na "wali", neno linalokuja kwanza ni ___.

misconceptions.cause: The child orders by how short or long the word is.
misconceptions.reveals: A short word that begins with a late letter.
misconceptions.help: Go by the letters of the alphabet, not by how long the word is.
misconceptions.feedback: Kamusi hupanga maneno kwa mpangilio wa alfabeti, si kwa urefu wa neno.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Goes from z back to a.

example.question: Kati ya "baba", "mto" na "zeze", neno linalokuja kwanza ni ___.

misconceptions.cause: The child reads the alphabet from the end.
misconceptions.reveals: First and last words asked in turn.
misconceptions.help: The alphabet begins with a.
misconceptions.feedback: Alfabeti huanza na a na kuishia na z. Neno lenye herufi ya mwanzo karibu na a hutangulia.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Does not know what a dictionary is for (takes it for a storybook or a book of pictures).
misconceptions.cause: The child has seen a dictionary but not used it.
misconceptions.reveals: The use of a dictionary asked directly.
misconceptions.help: What do you look for when you meet a word you do not know?
misconceptions.feedback: Kamusi ni kitabu chenye maneno na maana zake, yaliyopangwa kwa mpangilio wa alfabeti.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.mastery: Picks the pronoun (the word that stands in place of a noun: yeye, wao, sisi, huyu, hawa, yule, wale) that fits the person, number and nearness, without repeating the noun or choosing another word, in 8 of 10 new items.

misconceptions.error: Repeats the noun instead of using a pronoun.
misconceptions.cause: The child does not see that a pronoun stands in place of the name.
misconceptions.reveals: A second sentence that needs a pronoun, with the name among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask: which word saves us saying the name again?
misconceptions.feedback: Kiwakilishi husimama mahali pa nomino ili tusirudie jina: "Yeye" badala ya "Wanjiru".
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses a pronoun for one where there are many, or for many where there is one (yeye for wao).

example.question: Juma na Otieno ni marafiki. ___ wanacheza pamoja.

misconceptions.cause: The child does not count the people.
misconceptions.reveals: A pair of people with a one-person pronoun among the options.
misconceptions.help: Count the people. One is "yeye", many are "wao".
misconceptions.feedback: "Yeye" ni mtu mmoja. "Wao" ni watu wengi. Juma na Otieno ni wawili, kwa hiyo ni "wao".
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Swaps the person (mimi, wewe, yeye, sisi, nyinyi, wao).

example.question: Mimi na wewe ni marafiki. ___ tunasoma pamoja.

misconceptions.cause: The child knows the pronouns but not who is speaking.
misconceptions.reveals: A sentence about the speaker and the listener.
misconceptions.help: Does it include me, the speaker?
misconceptions.feedback: "Sisi" ni mimi na wengine. "Wao" ni watu wengine, bila mimi.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Swaps the near and the far one (huyu for yule, hawa for wale).

example.question: Angalia, ___ ni mwalimu wetu, ameketi karibu nami.

misconceptions.cause: The child does not take the distance into account.
misconceptions.reveals: A person who is close and a person who is far, with both words as options.
misconceptions.help: Is the person near you or far from you?
misconceptions.feedback: "Huyu" na "hawa" hutumika kwa walio karibu. "Yule" na "wale" hutumika kwa walio mbali.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.mastery: Tells a kitendawili from a methali, a nahau and an ordinary sentence, gives the opening words of riddling (Kitendawili! Tega!), and the answer to a known riddle, in 8 of 10 new items. Telling and guessing aloud is a teacher's check.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Takes a methali for a riddle.
misconceptions.cause: Both are short sayings.
misconceptions.reveals: A riddle and a methali.
misconceptions.help: A riddle hides an answer. Can you guess it?
misconceptions.feedback: Kitendawili huficha jibu na humtaka mtu kukitegua. Methali hutoa funzo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Takes a nahau for a riddle.
misconceptions.cause: Both can be a short phrase.
misconceptions.reveals: A riddle and a nahau.
misconceptions.help: Can you give an answer to it?
misconceptions.feedback: Nahau ni maneno yenye maana maalum. Kitendawili kina jibu la kutegua.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Takes an ordinary sentence for a riddle.
misconceptions.cause: The child does not see that a riddle hides the thing it describes.
misconceptions.reveals: A riddle and a plain sentence.
misconceptions.help: Does the text name the thing, or hide it?
misconceptions.feedback: Kitendawili hakitaji kitu moja kwa moja; hukielezea kwa fumbo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Does not know the words used when riddling (Kitendawili! Tega!).
misconceptions.cause: The child has heard a riddle told but not the fixed words.
misconceptions.reveals: The opening and the giving-up words.
misconceptions.help: What does the guesser say to say he is ready?
misconceptions.feedback: Mtegaji husema "Kitendawili!" na mtegua hujibu "Tega!". Akishindwa husema "Nipe mji."
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives a thing that shares one detail with the riddle but is not the answer.
misconceptions.cause: The child picks the first thing that comes to mind.
misconceptions.reveals: A riddle with plausible answers.
misconceptions.help: Test each answer against every part of the riddle.
misconceptions.feedback: Jibu la kitendawili lazima lilingane na kila sehemu yake.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kushirikiana na wenzake kujadili vipengele vya kuzingatia katika kusoma makala kwa ufasaha,
kusikiliza na kutazama mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa, mwanafunzi mwenzake au video za watu wanaosoma makala kwa ufasaha (k.v hotuba na habari),
kujadili na wenzake vipengele vya kuzingatia katika kusoma kwa ufasaha vilivyozingatiwa katika usomaji alioutazama,
kusoma kifungu cha hadithi kuhusu suala lengwa kwa kuzingatia matamshi bora akiwa na wenzake,
kusoma kifungu cha hadithi kuhusu suala lengwa kwa kuzingatia kiwango kifaacho cha sauti (k.v kiwango cha sauti na kiimbo),
kusoma kifungu cha hadithi kuhusu suala lengwa kwa kuzingatia kasi ifaayo (maneno sahihi yasiyopungua 60 kwa dakika) ili wenzake wamtolee maoni,
kusoma kifungu kwa kuambatanisha ishara zifaazo panapofaa anaposoma (k.v ishara za uso na mikono),

key_inquiry_questions: Unazingatia nini ili kuweza kusoma kifungu cha hadithi ipasavyo?

Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika kusoma kifungu cha hadithi.

Hamu ya ujifunzaji: mwanafunzi anapotafuta hadithi mbalimbali na kuzisoma kwa kuzingatia matamshi bora, kasi ifaayo na kiwango kifaacho cha sauti.

Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anapotunza vifaa vya kidijitali.

skills.name: Tambua vipengele vya kusoma kwa ufasaha
skills.mastery: Names what a fluent reader does (good pronunciation, a fitting voice, a fitting speed, a rest at the marks, signs that fit), without taking fast or loud for good, in 8 of 10 new items. Reading aloud itself is for a teacher to hear.
question_forms: choose what a good reader does

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Thinks that reading fast is reading well.

example.question: Ni nini kinachoonyesha kusoma kwa ufasaha?

misconceptions.cause: The child hears that good readers are quick.
misconceptions.reveals: Fast and fitting as options.
misconceptions.help: Can the listener follow every word?
misconceptions.feedback: Kasi ifaayo si haraka sana wala polepole sana: msikilizaji aelewe kila neno.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks that reading loud is reading well.

example.question: Sauti ipasavyo wakati wa kusoma ni ipi?

misconceptions.cause: The child takes loud for clear.
misconceptions.reveals: Loud and clear as options.
misconceptions.help: Is a shout the same as a clear voice?
misconceptions.feedback: Sauti ipasavyo inasikika wazi bila kupiga kelele wala kunong'ona.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Ignores the koma and the kikomo.
misconceptions.cause: The child reads the words and skips the marks.
misconceptions.reveals: A mark that asks for a rest.
misconceptions.help: What does the mark tell the reader to do?
misconceptions.feedback: Alama za uakifishi zinaonyesha mahali pa kupumzika: koma kidogo, kikomo muda mrefu zaidi.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tambua sehemu za tarakilishi zinazotumika kupigia chapa
skills.mastery: Names the part of a computer for typing and showing (kibodi, kipanya, skrini, kichapishi, the space key) and what each one does, in 8 of 10 new items. Using the computer is a practical task.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

skills.name: Hariri sentensi: herufi kubwa, kikomo, kiulizi, koma na alama ya hisi
skills.mastery: Chooses the sentence with the right capital letter, kikomo (full stop), kiulizi (question mark), koma and alama ya hisi (!), and finds the one mistake in a short note, in 8 of 10 new sentences.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Mixes the parts of a computer (kibodi, kipanya, skrini).
misconceptions.cause: The child knows the names but not what each is.
misconceptions.reveals: Parts asked by what they are used for.
misconceptions.help: What do you hold, press or look at?
misconceptions.feedback: Kibodi ina vitufe vya herufi na nambari. Kipanya husogeza kielekezi. Skrini huonyesha. Kichapishi huchapisha.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives the use of another part.
misconceptions.cause: The child has the right word for the wrong job.
misconceptions.reveals: The use of the part asked in turn.
misconceptions.help: What do you do with this part?
misconceptions.feedback: Kila sehemu ya tarakilishi ina kazi yake: skrini huonyesha, kichapishi huchapisha kwenye karatasi.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Starts a sentence or a name with a small letter.
misconceptions.cause: The child does not see the first letter.
misconceptions.reveals: The same sentence with a small and a capital letter.
misconceptions.help: What do we write first in a sentence?
misconceptions.feedback: Sentensi huanza kwa herufi kubwa, na majina ya pekee pia: Wanjiru, Nairobi.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Ends a question with a kikomo (.) instead of a kiulizi (?).
misconceptions.cause: The child ends every sentence with a full stop.
misconceptions.reveals: The same question with different marks.
misconceptions.help: Is the sentence asking?
misconceptions.feedback: Sentensi ya swali huisha kwa kiulizi (?). Sentensi ya kawaida huisha kwa kikomo (.).
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Leaves out the koma in a list, or puts it in the wrong place.
misconceptions.cause: The child does not pause the sentence where the list items end.
misconceptions.reveals: A list with and without koma.
misconceptions.help: Where would you rest your voice?
misconceptions.feedback: Koma hutenganisha vitu katika orodha: maembe, machungwa na ndizi.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses the wrong mark for a feeling (alama ya hisi !) or for a question.
misconceptions.cause: The child does not tell a feeling from a question.
misconceptions.reveals: An exclamation with ! and ?.
misconceptions.help: Is it asking, or showing a feeling?
misconceptions.feedback: Alama ya hisi (!) huonyesha hisia kama furaha au mshangao: Hongera! Kiulizi (?) huuliza.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Leaves out the mark at the end of the sentence.
misconceptions.cause: The child stops writing at the last word.
misconceptions.reveals: The same sentence with and without its closing mark.
misconceptions.help: How does a sentence end?
misconceptions.feedback: Kila sentensi huisha kwa alama: kikomo (.), kiulizi (?) au alama ya hisi (!).
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tambua na tumia viunganishi
skills.mastery: Picks the joining word (na, pia, kwa sababu, lakini, ili, au) that fits the meaning of two parts of a sentence, without choosing a noun or a verb or a joining word of another meaning, in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Picks a joining word of another meaning (kwa sababu for lakini, ili for au).

example.question: Alitaka kuogelea, ___ ziwa lilikuwa na mawimbi makali.

misconceptions.cause: The child picks a joining word without asking how the two parts are related.
misconceptions.reveals: Two parts that are in contrast, with the reason word among the options.
misconceptions.help: Do the two parts agree, or does the second go against the first?
misconceptions.feedback: Kila kiunganishi kina kazi: "lakini" kinaonyesha kinyume, "kwa sababu" kinatoa sababu, "ili" kinaonyesha kusudi, "na" kinaongeza.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks a noun or a verb for a joining word.
misconceptions.cause: The child chooses a word that is already in the sentence.
misconceptions.reveals: A gap between two names, with a noun among the options.
misconceptions.help: Which word joins the two names?
misconceptions.feedback: Kiunganishi huunganisha maneno au sentensi, kama "na", "lakini" na "kwa sababu". Si nomino wala kitenzi.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tambua na tumia vihusishi
skills.mastery: Picks the relating word (juu ya, chini ya, ndani ya, nje ya, karibu na, mbali na, kwa, kuliko) in a sentence, and chooses the -a of agreement (cha, vya, wa, ya, la) that matches the noun, in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Picks a noun, a verb or an adjective as the relating word.

example.question: Ni kihusishi kipi katika sentensi: "Kitabu kiko juu ya meza."

misconceptions.cause: The child picks the word that is easiest to see.
misconceptions.reveals: A sentence with a place word, with the nouns as options.
misconceptions.help: Which words tell where the book is in relation to the table?
misconceptions.feedback: Kihusishi hueleza uhusiano wa nomino na neno lingine, kama "juu ya", "chini ya" na "ndani ya". "Meza" ni nomino.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses the wrong -a of agreement for the noun (kitabu wa mwalimu, nyumba cha bibi).
misconceptions.cause: The child keeps one form for every noun.
misconceptions.reveals: Nouns of different classes before the same word.
misconceptions.help: Which class is the noun in? Kitabu is KI-VI, so cha.
misconceptions.feedback: Kihusishi cha "a" hubadilika kulingana na ngeli: kitabu cha, vitabu vya, mlango wa, milango ya, jina la, majina ya, nyumba ya.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Swaps place words that mean the opposite (juu ya for chini ya, ndani ya for nje ya).

example.question: Samaki wanaishi ___ ya maji, si nje yake.

misconceptions.cause: The child knows the words but not which way each points.
misconceptions.reveals: A sentence that says where, with the opposite word among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read the clue in the sentence: inside or outside?
misconceptions.feedback: "Ndani ya" na "nje ya" ni vinyume. "Juu ya" na "chini ya" ni vinyume pia.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.help: What does the other person feel? What would you say?
misconceptions.feedback: Kihisishi huonyesha hisia: "Pole!" kwa huzuni, "Hongera!" kwa mafanikio, "Samahani!" ukikosea, "Karibu!" kwa mgeni.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks a noun or a verb for an exclamation.

example.question: Hongera! Juma ameshinda mbio za shule. Ni kihisishi kipi?

misconceptions.cause: The child does not know the exclamation has the mark ! and shows a feeling.
misconceptions.reveals: A sentence that begins with an exclamation, with the other words as options.
misconceptions.help: Which word shows a feeling and carries the mark !?
misconceptions.feedback: Kihisishi kinaonyesha hisia na huandikwa pamoja na alama ya hisi (!). "Juma" ni nomino.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

kutumia maneno ya upole katika sentensi.

skills.name: Tambua na tumia maneno ya upole
skills.mastery: Picks the polite word or sentence (tafadhali, samahani, asante, pole, naomba) for the situation, and does not choose a command, in 8 of 10 new items. Using them aloud is a teacher's check.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Asks with a command and no polite word (Nipe maji!).
misconceptions.cause: The child does not hear the tone of the order.
misconceptions.reveals: A request and a command side by side.
misconceptions.help: Which one would you like to be asked?
misconceptions.feedback: Tunapoomba kitu tunatumia "tafadhali" na "naomba", si amri.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Swaps the polite words (asante for samahani).

example.question: Umemgonga mwenzako kwa bahati mbaya. Utasema "___."

misconceptions.cause: The child knows the words but not what each is for.
misconceptions.reveals: A situation with a thank-you, an apology and a request among the options.
misconceptions.help: What did you do, and what would you want to say?
misconceptions.feedback: "Samahani" husemwa ukikosea. "Asante" husemwa ukipewa kitu. "Pole" husemwa kwa aliyeumia.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Takes a plain sentence for a polite one.

example.question: Ni sentensi ipi ina neno la upole?

misconceptions.cause: The child does not look for the polite word.
misconceptions.reveals: Sentences with and without a polite word.
misconceptions.help: Which sentence has a word like tafadhali, samahani or asante?
misconceptions.feedback: Maneno ya upole ni kama tafadhali, samahani, asante, pole na naomba.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kutambua na kuzingatia hatua za kiusalama (k.m. kutowasiliana na watu asiowajua, kuwajibika anaposakura tovuti mbalimbali) kutoka kwenye chati au kwenye tarakilishi na mitandao,

kutafuta maana za maneno kuhusu suala lengwa kwenye kamusi au mtandaoni,
asikilize matamshi na maelezo kuhusu anachokisoma mtandaoni panapowezekana,

Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anapotunza vifaa vya kidijitali na kuzingatia mitandao salama.
Uadilifu: mwanafunzi anapotoa habari kwa mwalimu au mlezi apatapo ujumbe kutoka kwa watu asiowajua mtandoni.

kutambua na kuzingatia hatua za kiusalama katika matumizi ya vifaa vya kidijitali

skills.name: Zingatia hatua za kiusalama unapotumia kifaa cha kidijitali
skills.mastery: Picks the safe step for a phone, tablet or computer (keep the password secret, show an adult an unknown link, give no home address to a stranger, log out, use a safe site) and not the risky one, in 8 of 10 new situations.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Gives out a password or a private detail.

example.question: Rafiki anakuomba nenosiri la simu yako. Ufanye nini?

misconceptions.cause: The child thinks that sharing with a friend is harmless.
misconceptions.reveals: A friend or a stranger who asks.
misconceptions.help: Who should know the password?
misconceptions.feedback: Nenosiri na maelezo kama anwani ni siri yako. Usimpe mtu mwingine, hata rafiki.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Opens an unknown link or file.
misconceptions.cause: The child is curious.
misconceptions.reveals: A message with a link from a stranger.
misconceptions.help: Can you tell where the link leads?
misconceptions.feedback: Kiungo au faili usiyoijua inaweza kuwa hatari. Mwonyeshe mtu mzima kabla ya kuifungua.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses any site, or one that asks for private details.

example.question: Unatafuta kifungu cha kusoma mtandaoni. Utumie tovuti ipi?

misconceptions.cause: The child takes the first result.
misconceptions.reveals: A site that asks for a phone number or money.
misconceptions.help: Who said the site is safe?
misconceptions.feedback: Tumia tovuti salama zilizopendekezwa na mwalimu au mzazi. Tovuti inayoomba nambari ya simu au pesa si salama.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tambua sehemu za barua ya kirafiki
skills.mastery: Names the parts of a friendly letter in their order (anwani ya mwandishi, tarehe, salamu, mwili, hitimisho, jina) and what each holds, in 8 of 10 new items. Writing the letter is composition marking.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Puts the parts of a letter in the wrong order.

example.question: Barua ya kirafiki huanza kwa anwani ya mwandishi, kisha tarehe, kisha ___.

misconceptions.cause: The child knows the parts but not their order.
misconceptions.reveals: The parts of a letter asked in turn.
misconceptions.help: What comes after the date, and what before the end?
misconceptions.feedback: Barua ya kirafiki ina anwani ya mwandishi, tarehe, salamu, mwili, hitimisho na jina.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes the wrong greeting or closing for a friend (Wako mtiifu for Rafiki yako).

example.question: Hitimisho la barua ya kirafiki ni "___ ".

misconceptions.cause: The child mixes a friendly letter with an official one.
misconceptions.reveals: A friendly closing and an official one.
misconceptions.help: Who is the letter to: a friend or an officer?
misconceptions.feedback: Barua ya kirafiki huanza kwa "Mpendwa..." na kuisha kwa "Rafiki yako". "Wako mtiifu" ni ya barua rasmi.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes the address of the writer in the wrong place.

example.question: Anwani ya mwandishi huandikwa upande wa ___ juu.

misconceptions.cause: The child writes it where the greeting goes.
misconceptions.reveals: Left and right as options.
misconceptions.help: Which corner is the address of the writer?
misconceptions.feedback: Anwani ya mwandishi huandikwa upande wa kulia juu, kisha tarehe chini yake.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tumia ngeli ya A-WA kwa upatanisho wa kisarufi
skills.mastery: Knows that people and animals are in A-WA, gives a- for one and wa- for many (mtoto anacheza, watoto wanacheza), and makes the plural noun (mwalimu-walimu), in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.
Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Uses wa- for one person or a- for many people.
misconceptions.cause: The child does not count, or goes by the word before.
misconceptions.reveals: One and many in turn.
misconceptions.help: Count: one or many?
misconceptions.feedback: Nomino za ngeli ya A-WA hutumia a- kwa umoja na wa- kwa wingi: mtoto anaimba, watoto wanaimba.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives animals the prefix of things (ndege inaruka) instead of A-WA (ndege wanaruka).
misconceptions.cause: The child thinks only people are in A-WA.
misconceptions.reveals: Animals, birds and insects.
misconceptions.help: Is it alive and moving? People and animals take a- and wa-.
misconceptions.feedback: Watu na wanyama wote wako katika ngeli ya A-WA: paka anaruka, ndege wanaruka.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts a thing into A-WA (kitabu anasomwa).

example.question: Ni nomino ipi ni ya ngeli ya A-WA?

misconceptions.cause: The child picks a noun that begins with m- or a vowel and does not ask if it is a person or an animal.
misconceptions.reveals: A person among things.
misconceptions.help: Is it a person or an animal?
misconceptions.feedback: Ngeli ya A-WA ni ya watu na wanyama. Kitabu ni kitu, kiko katika ngeli ya KI-VI.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Makes a wrong plural noun for a person (vitoto, mitoto for watoto).
misconceptions.cause: The child puts on a prefix from another class.
misconceptions.reveals: Singular and plural nouns of people.
misconceptions.help: Which prefix do people take for many?
misconceptions.feedback: Wingi wa mtoto ni watoto, wa mwalimu ni walimu: m- hubadilika kuwa wa-.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tambua shairi, ubeti na mshororo
skills.mastery: Says what a shairi, an ubeti and a mshororo are, counts the beti and the mishororo in a short poem, and tells a poem from a paragraph by its shape, in 8 of 10 new items.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Swaps ubeti (a group of lines) and mshororo (one line).
misconceptions.cause: The child knows both words but not which is which.
misconceptions.reveals: Both words as options.
misconceptions.help: One line, or a group of lines?
misconceptions.feedback: Mshororo ni mstari mmoja wa shairi. Ubeti ni kundi la mishororo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Counts the lines of the whole poem for the lines of one ubeti (or the reverse).

example.question: Ubeti wa pili wa shairi hili una mishororo mingapi?

misconceptions.cause: The child counts all the lines.
misconceptions.reveals: A question about one ubeti with the total as an option.
misconceptions.help: Count only the lines of that ubeti.
misconceptions.feedback: Ubeti ni kundi moja la mishororo. Hesabu mishororo ya ubeti huo tu.

misconceptions.error: Takes a paragraph for a poem, or a poem for a paragraph.

example.question: Ni maandishi yapi ni shairi?

misconceptions.cause: The child does not look at the shape on the page.

skills.name: Tumia ngeli ya U-I kwa upatanisho wa kisarufi
skills.mastery: Knows nouns that belong to U-I (mti, mlango, mkono, mkoba, mguu), gives u- for one and i- for many, and makes the plural noun (mti-miti), without using the prefix of people, in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.
Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Uses i- with one noun of U-I.
misconceptions.cause: The child has fixed i- as the prefix of U-I.
misconceptions.reveals: One and many in turn.
misconceptions.help: Count: one or many?
misconceptions.feedback: Nomino za U-I hutumia u- kwa umoja: mti umeanguka. Hutumia i- kwa wingi: miti imeanguka.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses u- with many nouns of U-I.
misconceptions.cause: The child does not look at the number.
misconceptions.reveals: Plural nouns that begin with mi-.
misconceptions.help: Mi- tells you it is many.
misconceptions.feedback: Wingi wa mti ni miti, na kiambishi ni i-: miti imeanguka.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives a noun of U-I the prefix of people (mti anaanguka).
misconceptions.cause: The child sees m- and thinks of mtoto and mwalimu.
misconceptions.reveals: U-I nouns that begin with m- like people nouns.
misconceptions.help: Is it a person? A tree and a door are things.
misconceptions.feedback: Mti na mlango ni vitu, si watu. Vinatumia u- na i-, si a- na wa-.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts a noun of another class in U-I.

example.question: Ni nomino ipi ni ya ngeli ya U-I?

misconceptions.cause: The child sees m- and takes any noun that begins with it.
misconceptions.reveals: Nouns that begin with m- from different classes.
misconceptions.help: Is it a person or an animal? Then it is A-WA, not U-I.
misconceptions.feedback: Mtoto ni mtu, kwa hiyo yuko A-WA. Mti ni kitu na uko U-I.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Makes the plural noun with a prefix of another class (mamti, wamlango for miti, milango).
misconceptions.cause: The child puts on a prefix from another class.
misconceptions.reveals: Nouns of U-I in the plural.
misconceptions.help: m- becomes mi- for things of this class.
misconceptions.feedback: Wingi wa nomino za U-I huanza kwa mi-: mti-miti, mlango-milango, mkono-mikono, mguu-miguu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Elewa msamiati wa shairi la taifa
skills.mastery: Gives the meaning of the words of a poem about the nation (bendera, taifa, uhuru, shujaa, mshikamano, amani) and uses them in a sentence, without choosing a look-alike or an opposite word, in 8 of 10 new items. Reciting is a teacher's check.

misconceptions.error: Picks a word that looks or sounds like the word.
misconceptions.cause: The child goes by the sound.
misconceptions.reveals: A look-alike word as an option.
misconceptions.help: Say what each word means.
misconceptions.feedback: Maneno yanaweza kusikika sawa na yasiwe na maana sawa. Taifa ni nchi na watu wake.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks a word of the same family of ideas.
misconceptions.cause: The child picks an idea close to the nation.
misconceptions.reveals: Another symbol of the nation as an option.
misconceptions.help: What can you see, touch and hoist?
misconceptions.feedback: Bendera ni kitambaa chenye rangi kinachoonyesha nchi. Wimbo wa taifa ni wimbo rasmi wa nchi.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks the opposite.
misconceptions.cause: The child knows the topic but not which way it points.
misconceptions.reveals: The opposite meaning as an option.
misconceptions.help: Does the word mean the thing is there, or not?
misconceptions.feedback: Amani ni hali ya utulivu bila vita. Vita ni kinyume cha amani.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Elewa ujumbe wa makala
skills.mastery: Answers questions about a short article (makala) from what it says, and gives its main message, without choosing a detail for the message or an answer from outside the article, in 8 of 10 new questions.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Answers from what the child knows, not from the article.

example.question: Kwa mujibu wa makala, maji yachemshwe kwa muda gani?

misconceptions.cause: The child gives the figure he has heard.
misconceptions.reveals: A likely figure that the article does not give.
misconceptions.help: Point to the sentence in the article.
misconceptions.feedback: Jibu la swali la makala liko ndani ya makala. Tafuta sentensi inayolisema.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives a detail for the main message of the article.

example.question: Ujumbe mkuu wa makala ni upi?
example.correct_answer: Tunapaswa kunywa maji safi na salama.

misconceptions.cause: The child takes one sentence.
misconceptions.reveals: A detail and a message as options.

skills.name: Tumia ngeli ya LI-YA kwa upatanisho wa kisarufi
skills.mastery: Knows nouns that belong to LI-YA (jiwe, jicho, tunda, embe, dirisha, jina), gives li- for one and ya- for many, and makes the plural noun with ma- (jiwe-mawe, tunda-matunda), in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Uses ya- with one noun of LI-YA.
misconceptions.cause: The child has fixed ya- as the prefix of LI-YA.
misconceptions.reveals: One and many in turn.
misconceptions.help: Count: one or many?
misconceptions.feedback: Nomino za LI-YA hutumia li- kwa umoja: jiwe limeanguka. Hutumia ya- kwa wingi: mawe yameanguka.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses li- with many nouns of LI-YA.
misconceptions.cause: The child does not see that ma- tells it is many.
misconceptions.reveals: Plural nouns that begin with ma-.
misconceptions.help: Ma- tells you it is many.
misconceptions.feedback: Wingi wa jiwe ni mawe, na kiambishi ni ya-: mawe yameanguka.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Makes the plural with the wrong form (majiwe, majicho for mawe, macho).
misconceptions.cause: The child adds ma- and keeps ji-.
misconceptions.reveals: Nouns that begin with ji-.
misconceptions.help: ji- becomes ma-: jiwe-mawe, jicho-macho.
misconceptions.feedback: Nomino za LI-YA zinazoanza na ji- hupoteza ji- katika wingi: jiwe-mawe, jicho-macho. Nyingine hupata ma-: tunda-matunda.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts a noun of another class in LI-YA.

example.question: Ni nomino ipi ni ya ngeli ya LI-YA?

misconceptions.cause: The child goes by the first letters only.
misconceptions.reveals: Nouns from other classes with a look-alike beginning.
misconceptions.help: Does it form its plural with ma-?
misconceptions.feedback: Kiti kiko katika ngeli ya KI-VI (viti). Jiwe liko LI-YA (mawe).
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives a noun of LI-YA the prefix of another class (kimeanguka for limeanguka).
misconceptions.cause: The child does not tell which class the noun belongs to.
misconceptions.reveals: Several prefixes as options.
misconceptions.help: Which class has the plural with ma-? Its prefixes are li- and ya-.
misconceptions.feedback: Nomino za LI-YA hutumia li- kwa umoja na ya- kwa wingi, si ki-, vi-, u- wala i-.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tambua na eleza maana ya nahau za maadili na uraia
skills.mastery: Tells a nahau from other sayings and gives what it means (kupiga moyo konde, kujikaza kisabuni, kula kiapo, kukata tamaa), without taking it word for word, in 8 of 10 new items. Using it aloud is a teacher's check.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Takes the nahau word for word.

example.question: Nahau "kupiga moyo konde" ina maana gani?

misconceptions.cause: The child reads the words and not the meaning.
misconceptions.reveals: A literal meaning as an option.
misconceptions.help: Can the words mean what they say?
misconceptions.feedback: Nahau ni maneno yenye maana tofauti na maneno yenyewe.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives the meaning of another nahau.
misconceptions.cause: The child knows the topic but mixes the phrases.
misconceptions.reveals: Meanings of two nahau on the same topic.
misconceptions.help: Which words of the phrase does the meaning explain?
misconceptions.feedback: Kila nahau ina maana yake. Linganisha maneno ya nahau na maana kabla ya kuchagua.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Takes a methali or an ordinary phrase for a nahau.
misconceptions.cause: The child does not tell a nahau from a methali.
misconceptions.reveals: A nahau among methali and phrases.
misconceptions.help: Is it a short phrase that is not a whole saying with a lesson?
misconceptions.feedback: Nahau ni kifungu kifupi chenye maana maalum. Methali ni sentensi nzima yenye funzo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Changes a word of the nahau (kupiga moyo kubwa for kupiga moyo konde).
misconceptions.cause: The child remembers the sense but not the exact words.
misconceptions.reveals: A gap in a nahau with plausible words.
misconceptions.help: Which word goes with the others in this phrase?
misconceptions.feedback: Nahau hutumia maneno yale yale: kupiga moyo konde, kujikaza kisabuni, kula kiapo, kukata tamaa.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia mtandao kupata matini ya kusoma.

Uwazaji kina na utatuzi wa matatizo: mwanafunzi anaposimulia wenzake kuhusu matini aliyosoma na kupasha ujumbe uliotumiwa.

sub_strands.sub_strand: Insha ya Maelezo (Theme 7: Matunda na mimea)
learning_experiences: kutambua vifungu vya maelezo vilivyoandikwa kwenye matini mbalimbali au tarakilishi,
kushiriki na wenzake kujadili mada na muundo wa insha ya maelezo,
kuandaa vidokezo vitakavyomwongoza kuandika insha yake,

kuandika insha ya maelezo akizingatia suala lengwa (k.v upanzi wa miti na mimea, utunzaji wa mimea, shamba la matunda n.k) hasa akizingatia vivumishi na vielezi vifaavyo kutoa picha dhahiri kuhusu anachokielezea,

kuandika insha ya maelezo mtandaoni na kuisambaza kwa wenzake na mwalimu ili waisome na kuitathmini,
kuwasomea wenzake insha aliyoandika ili waisikilize na kuitathmini.

Ubunifu: mwanafunzi anapoandika insha ya maelezo akizingatia suala lengwa.

skills.name: Tambua visawe
skills.mastery: Picks the word with the same meaning (haraka-upesi, shida-taabu, furaha-raha) and does not choose a look-alike, an opposite or a related word, in 8 of 10 new items. Using visawe aloud is a teacher's check.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Picks the opposite.
misconceptions.cause: The child knows the topic but not which way it points.
misconceptions.reveals: The opposite as an option.
misconceptions.help: Same meaning, or opposite?
misconceptions.feedback: Kisawe ni neno lenye maana sawa. Kinyume cha furaha ni huzuni, si kisawe.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks a word that looks or sounds like the word.
misconceptions.cause: The child goes by the first letters.
misconceptions.reveals: A look-alike word as an option.
misconceptions.help: Say what each word means.
misconceptions.feedback: Maneno yanaweza kuanza kwa herufi zilezile na yasiwe na maana sawa. Kisawe cha haraka ni upesi.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks a related word that is not the same in meaning.
misconceptions.cause: The child picks a word that goes with the idea.
misconceptions.reveals: A related word as an option.
misconceptions.help: Can you put it in place of the word, with the same meaning?
misconceptions.feedback: Kisawe kinaweza kuchukua mahali pa neno bila kubadilisha maana. Tajiri na mkwasi wana maana sawa.

skills.name: Tambua mchezo wa kuigiza, mhusika na maelekezo
skills.mastery: Tells a short play (igizo) from a story by its shape (the name of the speaker, a colon, the words said), names the speaker of a line, and finds the stage direction in brackets, in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Takes a line of a story for a line of a play (or the reverse).

example.question: Ni kipi kati ya hivi kinatoka kwenye mchezo wa kuigiza?

misconceptions.cause: The child does not see the name and the colon.
misconceptions.reveals: A play line and a story line side by side.
misconceptions.help: Does the line begin with a name and a colon?
misconceptions.feedback: Igizo huonyesha jina la mhusika, nukta mbili, kisha maneno anayosema. Hadithi huelezwa na msimulizi.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Takes the words in brackets for words that are said.
misconceptions.cause: The child reads everything on the page as speech.
misconceptions.reveals: A stage direction among spoken lines.
misconceptions.help: What does the actor do, and what does he say?
misconceptions.feedback: Maelekezo ya jukwaani yako kwenye mabano. Yanamwonyesha muigizaji afanye nini, si aseme nini.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Names the wrong speaker of a line.

example.question: Nani alisema, "Nipe kilo mbili za unga"?

misconceptions.cause: The child goes by the name closest to the line.
misconceptions.reveals: A line next to the name of another speaker.
misconceptions.help: The name before the colon is the speaker.
misconceptions.feedback: Jina lililo mbele ya nukta mbili ndilo la mhusika anayesema mstari huo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Answers from what the child knows, not from the play.
misconceptions.cause: The child gives a likely answer and does not look in the play.
misconceptions.reveals: A likely answer that the play does not give.
misconceptions.help: Point to the line in the play that says it.
misconceptions.feedback: Jibu la swali la igizo liko ndani ya igizo. Tafuta mstari unaolisema.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tambua na tumia kauli za kutenda, kutendea na kutendwa
skills.mastery: Tells the three verb forms apart (kutenda: andika, kutendea: andikia, done for someone, kutendwa: andikwa, done to the thing) and picks the one a sentence needs, in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Leaves the verb in its base form where someone is helped (anaandika for anamwandikia).
misconceptions.cause: The child does not see that the verb has to show for whom.
misconceptions.reveals: A sentence with a person who benefits.
misconceptions.help: Is it done for someone? Then the verb ends in -ia or -ea.
misconceptions.feedback: Kauli ya kutendea huonyesha kitendo kinafanyiwa mtu: anawaandikia, anampikia, anamsomea.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Leaves the verb active where the thing is done to (barua imeandika na mwalimu).
misconceptions.cause: The child does not see that the thing, not the person, is the subject.
misconceptions.reveals: A sentence that begins with the thing that was done.
misconceptions.help: Does the thing do it, or is it done to the thing? Then -wa.
misconceptions.feedback: Kauli ya kutendwa huonyesha kitu kimefanyiwa kitendo: barua imeandikwa, chai imepikwa.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Mixes -ia (for someone) and -wa (done to the thing).
misconceptions.cause: The endings look alike and the child does not ask what the verb says.
misconceptions.reveals: Sentences that need -wa or -ia in turn.
misconceptions.help: Ask: for someone, or done to the thing?
misconceptions.feedback: Kutendea (-ia, -ea) ni "kwa ajili ya mtu". Kutendwa (-wa) ni "kinatendwa na mtu".
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tambua miktadha isiyo rasmi na lugha yake
skills.mastery: Tells an informal setting (with a friend, at play, at home) from a formal one (a speech, an interview, a meeting) and picks the words that fit it, in 8 of 10 new items. Using them aloud is a teacher's check.

misconceptions.error: Takes a formal setting for an informal one.

example.question: Ni mazungumzo yapi si rasmi?
example.wrong_answer: hotuba ya mwalimu mkuu kwenye gwaride

misconceptions.cause: The child does not ask who is talking to whom.
misconceptions.reveals: A speech or an interview among settings with a friend.
misconceptions.help: Who is speaking to whom, and where?
misconceptions.feedback: Mazungumzo yasiyo rasmi ni ya marafiki, nyumbani au wakati wa kucheza. Hotuba na mahojiano ni rasmi.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.help: Would you say it to a friend at play?

skills.name: Tambua na tumia vinyume vya nomino
skills.mastery: Gives the true opposite of a noun (usiku-mchana, rafiki-adui, furaha-huzuni, tajiri-maskini) and does not choose a related word or a word of the same meaning, in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.
Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Picks a related word, not the opposite (usiku-jioni, rafiki-ndugu).
misconceptions.cause: The child picks a word of the same family of ideas.
misconceptions.reveals: A related word as an option.
misconceptions.help: Is it the opposite, or only near it?
misconceptions.feedback: Kinyume ni neno lenye maana kinyume kabisa: usiku-mchana. "Jioni" iko karibu na usiku lakini si kinyume.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks a word of the same meaning (furaha-raha).
misconceptions.cause: The child mixes the opposite with the synonym.
misconceptions.reveals: A synonym as an option.
misconceptions.help: Same meaning or opposite?
misconceptions.feedback: "Raha" ina maana sawa na furaha. Kinyume cha furaha ni huzuni.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives the other word of a pair in the wrong place (mgeni-rafiki for mgeni-mwenyeji).
misconceptions.cause: The child takes a word that goes with the idea.
misconceptions.reveals: A word that goes with the noun but is not its opposite.
misconceptions.help: Who is the visitor and who receives him?
misconceptions.feedback: Mgeni ni anayetembelea, na mwenyeji ni anayepokea. Ni vinyume.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tambua na tumia tashbihi za kimo na umbo
skills.mastery: Gives the usual comparison for height, size and shape (mrefu kama twiga, mnene kama kiboko, mkubwa kama ndovu) and says it is a simile because of kama, without taking it word for word, in 8 of 10 new items. Using it aloud is a teacher's check.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Gives the wrong animal or thing in the simile (mrefu kama sungura).

example.question: Mtu mrefu sana ni mrefu kama ___.

misconceptions.cause: The child knows the idea but not the usual comparison.
misconceptions.reveals: A simile with plausible animals as options.
misconceptions.help: Which animal do we say is tall?
misconceptions.feedback: Tashbihi hutumia ulinganisho wa kawaida: mrefu kama twiga, mnene kama kiboko, mkubwa kama ndovu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Leaves out kama, and says "Yeye ni twiga" as a simile.
misconceptions.cause: The child mixes a simile with a metaphor.
misconceptions.reveals: A simile and a metaphor as options.
misconceptions.help: A simile has the word kama.
misconceptions.feedback: Tashbihi hulinganisha kwa kutumia kama: mrefu kama twiga. "Yeye ni twiga" ni sitiari.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Takes the simile word for word (the person is really a giraffe).

example.question: "Baba ni mrefu kama twiga" maana yake nini?

misconceptions.cause: The child does not read the comparison as a way to describe.
misconceptions.reveals: A meaning question for a simile.
misconceptions.help: What is the animal used to show?
misconceptions.feedback: Tashbihi inaelezea kwa kulinganisha. "Mrefu kama twiga" ina maana mtu ni mrefu sana.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tambua na tumia nyakati: -li-, -na- na -ta-
skills.mastery: Uses -li- for what happened before (jana alisoma), -na- for now (anasoma) and -ta- for what will happen (atasoma), following the time word, and gives the right person prefix, in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Uses -na- for every time, whatever the time word.
misconceptions.cause: The child has fixed -na- as the way to make a verb.
misconceptions.reveals: Time words (jana, kesho) next to -na-.
misconceptions.help: Read the time word first: jana, now, or kesho?
misconceptions.feedback: Wakati uliopita unatumia -li-: jana alisoma. Uliopo -na-: sasa anasoma. Ujao -ta-: kesho atasoma.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Swaps -li- and -ta- (kesho alisoma).
misconceptions.cause: The child knows the markers but not which time each is for.
misconceptions.reveals: Past and future time words in turn.
misconceptions.help: Has it happened, or will it happen?
misconceptions.feedback: -li- ni kwa yaliyotokea. -ta- ni kwa yatakayotokea.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Keeps the tense right and changes the person prefix (wanasoma for tunasoma).

example.question: Chagua kitenzi: Jana sisi ___ kwa basi.

misconceptions.cause: The child looks at the tense and not at the person.
misconceptions.reveals: The same verb with different persons.
misconceptions.help: Who is it? Sisi is tu-.
misconceptions.feedback: Kitenzi kinahitaji nafsi na wakati: sisi tulisafiri, wao walisafiri, mimi nilisafiri.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Only adds ha- or si- and keeps the tense marker (hanasoma, sinasoma).
misconceptions.cause: The child does not know that the marker changes in the negative.
misconceptions.reveals: A negative made by only adding ha- or si-.
misconceptions.help: In the present negative, -na- goes and the verb ends in -i.
misconceptions.feedback: Kukanusha wakati uliopo: -na- huondolewa na kitenzi huishia -i: nasoma-sisomi, anasoma-hasomi.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Keeps -li- or -ta- after ha- (halipika, hatapika for hakupika).
misconceptions.cause: The child puts ha- in front and leaves the rest.
misconceptions.reveals: A past verb with ha- put in front.
misconceptions.help: -li- becomes -ku- in the past negative.
misconceptions.feedback: Wakati uliopita ukikanushwa, -li- hubadilika kuwa -ku-: alipika-hakupika.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives the negative of another time (hasomi for hakusoma).
misconceptions.cause: The child negates the verb but does not keep the time.
misconceptions.reveals: Negatives of the three times side by side.
misconceptions.help: Which time was the first sentence in?
misconceptions.feedback: Ukanushaji huhifadhi wakati: uliopita hawakuimba, uliopo hawaimbi, ujao hawataimba.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Takes a positive verb for a negative one.
misconceptions.cause: The child does not look for the ha-, si-, hu- or ku-.
misconceptions.reveals: A negative and a positive verb together.
misconceptions.help: Which verb says that it did not, does not or will not happen?
misconceptions.feedback: Neno lililokanushwa linaonyesha kwamba kitendo hakifanyiki: hasomi, hakusoma, hatasoma.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher
